journal_name: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters

abstracts.abstract: This letter presents a novel information-theoretic framework for hyperspectral image classification that fundamentally reconceptualizes the relationship between spectral signatures and spatial context. Traditional approaches treat spectral and spatial features as complementary but separable components, whereas the proposed paradigm establishes an intrinsic coupling mechanism through which spatial neighborhood structure dynamically modulates spectral band importance. We derive novel entropy-based measures that quantify the mutual information flow between spectral bands conditioned on spatial configuration, enabling a principled quantification of feature relevance that adapts to local image statistics. The theoretical analysis reveals that optimal feature selection depends not on global statistics but on spatially-varying information geometry. Based on this insight, we develop a classification framework that computes spatially-adaptive spectral weighting matrices derived from local entropy landscapes. Experiments on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets demonstrate that this paradigm achieves classification accuracy improvements of 3-7% over state-of-the-art methods, particularly in regions with complex land cover transitions. The proposed framework establishes a new theoretical direction for hyperspectral image processing by demonstrating that spatial context should be integrated at the fundamental information-theoretic level rather than treated as post-processing enhancement. This paradigm shift provides a rigorous foundation for understanding why spatial-spectral methods succeed and enables principled design of future classification approaches.

This letter presents an enhanced theoretical analysis of sparse representation-based classification for SAR image interpretation, addressing critical limitations in existing formulations regarding noise modeling and dictionary coherence. Previous sparse coding approaches to SAR image classification assume additive Gaussian noise and treat dictionary atoms as independent, conditions that poorly reflect the multiplicative speckle noise and high inter-class correlation inherent to SAR data. We develop a robust sparse recovery framework that incorporates Gamma-distributed noise modeling and introduces coherence-aware dictionary learning with theoretical recovery guarantees. The mathematical analysis establishes tightened bounds on reconstruction error that account for the statistical properties of SAR backscatter coefficients. Furthermore, we derive sufficient conditions for successful classification under speckle corruption, revealing that existing theoretical guarantees are overly pessimistic for SAR applications. Based on these theoretical insights, we propose a modified optimization formulation with adapted regularization terms that align with SAR noise statistics. Experimental validation on TerraSAR-X and Sentinel-1 datasets demonstrates classification accuracy improvements of 4-12% over conventional sparse representation methods, with more substantial gains observed under severe speckle conditions. The theoretical contributions advance understanding of sparse recovery in SAR-specific noise environments and provide principled guidance for parameter selection in operational applications.

This letter introduces a novel dual-modal LiDAR-RADAR fusion architecture that fundamentally redefines sensor integration for autonomous environmental monitoring. Conventional fusion systems treat LiDAR and RADAR as complementary sensors processed through sequential or late-fusion strategies, which fail to exploit the intrinsic physical complementarity of these sensing modalities. The proposed architecture implements a physically-grounded cross-modal attention mechanism that operates at the signal level before feature extraction, enabling direct interaction between raw point cloud data and radar signal streams. The system architecture comprises three novel components: a synchronized acquisition module that aligns LiDAR point clouds with radar chirp signals at the hardware level, a cross-modal feature projector that establishes learnable correspondences between geometric (LiDAR) and electromagnetic (RADAR) representations, and an adaptive weighting network that dynamically adjusts fusion ratios based on environmental conditions. Unlike previous approaches that require manual parameter tuning for different weather scenarios, the proposed system automatically adapts fusion behavior by interpreting cross-modal consistency signals. Field experiments conducted across diverse environmental conditions including fog, rain, and dust demonstrate robust performance with detection accuracy degradation of less than 5% under moderate visibility reduction, compared to 15-30% degradation for LiDAR-only systems. The architecture enables real-time operation at 20 Hz processing frequency, making it suitable for operational environmental monitoring platforms.

This letter presents a significantly enhanced system for real-time satellite data processing that addresses critical operational limitations in existing Earth observation platforms. Current operational systems face fundamental trade-offs between spatial resolution, spectral coverage, and processing latency, making it challenging to simultaneously achieve high-fidelity land cover classification and timely environmental monitoring. The proposed system introduces a cascaded processing pipeline with novel module designs that substantially improve computational efficiency without compromising classification accuracy. The core architectural improvements include a hierarchical tile-based processing framework that enables parallel execution across distributed computing nodes, a memory-efficient feature extraction module using progressive resolution streaming, and a lightweight classification head optimized for edge deployment. We design the system to process Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery at full resolution (10m) with an end-to-end latency under 30 seconds, representing a four-fold improvement over existing operational systems. The classification accuracy on the developed system achieves 94.2% overall accuracy on land cover mapping tasks, demonstrating that the efficiency improvements do not come at the expense of classification quality. The system has been deployed on a cloud-based processing infrastructure serving regional environmental monitoring agencies, where it processes approximately 500 scenes daily while maintaining sub-minute latency for alert generation. The engineering contributions provide a scalable blueprint for transitioning advanced remote sensing algorithms to operational Earth observation systems.
